title: The 3:00 AM Seam
credit: Revised from the film's own lines (film/story.json) for a first-time player.

intro.kicker: Design studio · 3:00 am · the test is filmed at eight
intro.text: Your team's paper pavilion has to open on camera in five hours: a canopy that spreads like a fan. One of its ribs keeps cracking. The glue needs from half past four to set, so there's one more try.

cast.name: Mara
cast.role: cut a spare rib at midnight; her fellowship footage is due at noon

cast.name: Julian
cast.role: designed the pavilion; it's his rib that keeps failing

prompt: One try left before the glue sets. Which rib gets it?

setup.line: The canopy opens. A rib bends, the paper louvres catch, and the whole thing folds in on itself.

setup.speaker: Julian
setup.direction: exhausted, flat, close to giving up

setup.speaker: Mara
setup.line: The louvres catch every time that rib bends. It isn't going to hold, Julian.

setup.speaker: Mara
setup.line: I cut a spare at midnight, just in case. It'll fit in forty minutes.

setup.speaker: Mara
setup.line: And I'll be straight with you. My fellowship application closes at noon. This test is my footage.
setup.direction: honest about her own stake, slightly uncomfortable saying it

setup.speaker: Julian
setup.line: I know. I just wanted to be here when my design moved. Not a copy of it.
Julian rubs his eyes. He hasn't slept. He keeps hold of his pencil.

setup.speaker: Mara
setup.line: Ren, you're leading this. I need your call.

setup.speaker: You
setup.line: One try before the glue sets. Mara's spare, or we fix Julian's.

backup.speaker: You
backup.line: We'll use the spare. Julian, take a break. You've been up all night.

backup.speaker: Julian
backup.line: Yeah. Okay. Just keep my drawing out. Please.
backup.direction: hurt but too tired to argue

backup.line: Mara fits the clean rib while you hold it steady. Julian's cracked one lies on the table.

backup.speaker: You
backup.line: On Mara's rib. Yours is still on the table.

backup.speaker: Julian
backup.line: I wanted to see mine move.

backup.speaker: You
backup.line: Then that's our next test. Yours. Before we record, show me your drawing.

backup.speaker: Mara
backup.line: Start with the rib. Show us where it cracks.

repair.line: You reach for Julian's cracked rib and hold it steady.

repair.speaker: You
repair.line: Let's splint his. Together. Julian, show me where it gives.

repair.speaker: Mara
repair.line: Then I need both of you on the canopy with me. Now.
repair.direction: tense, swallowing her worry, getting on with it

repair.speaker: Julian
repair.line: Hold it there. Don't let it twist.

repair.speaker: Mara
repair.line: Half of it. The other half still sticks.

repair.speaker: You
repair.line: That was my call. We'll show the jam on camera, and say what worked.

repair.speaker: Mara
repair.line: Not the footage I wanted. But it's honest.

lesson: Deadlines and ownership pull against each other. Whichever you choose, say out loud whose work you're putting first, and why.

backup.title: You chose the spare.
backup.kept: The deadline. The canopy moved on camera, and Mara has her footage.
backup.cost: Julian's own design stayed on the table, and he wasn't the one who saw it move.
backup.ask: How will you make sure Julian's rib gets its test?

repair.title: You fixed his original, together.
repair.kept: Julian's design, and what the team learned by fixing it.
repair.cost: A canopy that only half works on camera, and Mara's best footage.
repair.ask: What do you owe Mara now?
